title: On classic n-universal quadratic forms over dyadic local fields
author: Zilong He
citation: Zilong He, On classic n-universal quadratic forms over dyadic local fields, manuscripta math. 174 (2024), 559-595

comparisonSources.description: 33-page arXiv v3 comparison copy, revised 25 December 2025 after publication

formalizedScope: Theorem 1.1 proved equivalence for every source rank and n >= 2, with both parity branches
Classic maximality and existence of classic-maximal over-lattices
Local BONG proof chain in Sections 2-6, with source differences recorded separately
Theorem 1.5 local implication for every n >= 1 and Corollary 6.3 even branch
Section 7 ambient exhaustion and Lemma 7.4 even-rank testing equivalence
Lemma 7.7 and all three clauses of Lemma 7.10 on the literal published even table
Theorem 1.3(i) and its even-rank literal deletion minimality conclusion in Theorem 1.3(iii)
Kernel-checked refutation of the literal Lemma 7.1(ii) disjunction when e > 1
excludedScope: Theorem 1.3(ii), odd-rank minimality through Lemma 7.11, and unconditional published numerical counts without a proved counting-law instance
Theorem 1.5 number-field localization and global unramifiedness/discriminant conclusion
Literal Lemma 7.1(ii) and downstream claims requiring an unresolved source correction
Global consequences and independent human semantic sign-off
reviewNotice: Theorem 1.1 has a checked proof, not merely a proposition encoding. The complete n >= 1 local-field implication underlying Theorem 1.5 is proved, including its unary branch; its number-field localization and global discriminant clause are not. The literal even-rank family now satisfies the testing equivalence and row-by-row deletion minimality required by Theorem 1.3(i),(iii). The odd branch remains incomplete because the false literal Lemma 7.1(ii) is disclosed and refuted, not assumed or silently repaired. Grade C describes partial whole-paper coverage and is not a whole-paper certificate. The post-publication arXiv v3 copy is non-authoritative.
